description: A publisher groups the character records attributed to it; a character's publishing context is meaningless without its publisher entry.
A race entry groups the characters classified under it; the classification is part of the character record.
An alignment entry groups the characters classified under it; the classification is part of the character record.
A gender entry groups the characters classified under it; the classification is part of the character record.
A score is a reading of one named attribute; without its attribute entry a score has no meaning.
A score belongs to exactly one character profile and is meaningless without that character.

connection_condition: superhero.eye_colour_id resolves against colour.id, so eye-colour values are a subset of the colour vocabulary
description: Eye colour is a specific kind of colour: every eye-colour value is drawn from the shared colour vocabulary, with no eye-specific values of its own.

connection_condition: superhero.hair_colour_id resolves against colour.id, so hair-colour values are a subset of the colour vocabulary
description: Hair colour is a specific kind of colour: every hair-colour value is drawn from the shared colour vocabulary, with no hair-specific values of its own.

connection_condition: superhero.skin_colour_id resolves against colour.id, so skin-colour values are a subset of the colour vocabulary
description: Skin colour is a specific kind of colour: every skin-colour value is drawn from the shared colour vocabulary, with no skin-specific values of its own.

connection_condition: superhero.eye_colour_id, superhero.hair_colour_id and superhero.skin_colour_id each resolve against colour.id
description: Each character carries up to three independent colour facets - eye, hair and skin - that all draw on one shared colour vocabulary; the facets are not interchangeable.

connection_condition: hero_power.hero_id corresponds to superhero.id and hero_power.power_id corresponds to superpower.id
description: Characters possess superpowers through a many-to-many association; a power is an independent vocabulary entry shared by many characters rather than a component of one.
Superpower count is derived by counting the distinct powers associated with a character; no stored column holds it.
The overall attribute score is derived by aggregating a character's six attribute scores; no stored total exists.
Hero count is derived by counting distinct character records; repeated superhero_name values do not reduce the count.

connection_condition: superhero.full_name and race.race use '-' whereas gender.gender, alignment.alignment, colour.colour and publisher.publisher_name use 'N/A', 'No Colour' or an empty string
description: Both placeholders express the same business concept - 'value unknown or not applicable' - in different physical vocabularies, so excluding one implies excluding the other.
